children: U.S. diesel prices hit a record-high $5.85 a gallon, according to AAA, and with U.S. refineries running flat out there's little more they can do at the margin to help ease the tightness in global products supply, BCA Research's chief commodities strategist Roukaya Ibrahim says. U.S. refineries operated at 98% of capacity last week, the EIA reported. Unlike China, which is giving priority to domestic crude supply, in the U.S. the energy producers are much more responsive to market conditions, she says. "Because the crack spread is wide, that really does improve their profit margins, so refineries are taking advantage of that." (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
